visible_observation: The headline 'ONE SPARK IS ENOUGH' is set in a heavy, geometric sans-serif font with uniform weight and standard spacing. It is positioned in the upper-left corner, floating in negative space, completely detached from the diagonal fire line graphic. The required instructional text ('Check conditions...') is entirely absent from the composition.
critique: The typography is passive and generic; it acts as a label rather than a structural element of the design. By using a standard, heavy weight, the text fails to convey the 'spark' or 'danger' implied by the message. It sits statically in the corner rather than interacting with the dynamic diagonal energy of the fire line. The absence of the secondary text leaves the poster without a call to action, rendering the visual metaphor incomplete.
revision: Replace the static sans-serif with a tall, condensed typeface (e.g., Druk Wide or similar) to create a vertical tension that mirrors the rising smoke. Align the text to the right edge of the canvas, stacking it so the bottom of the letters interacts with the top of the fire line, creating a visual 'burn' or shadow effect. Add the missing instructional text in a smaller, high-contrast weight at the bottom right to balance the composition.
protected_strength: The high-contrast color palette (deep blue vs. glowing orange) and the effective use of the diagonal fire line to divide the composition must be preserved.
